title: How a Circular Saw Works in 60 Seconds 🪚⚙️ #shorts
description:
A standard circular saw spins a 7¼-inch blade at around 5,500 RPM. Carbide-tipped teeth chip the wood while gullets carry sawdust out, the blade cuts upward from below, and a spring-loaded guard covers it when you're done. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#circularsaw #woodworking #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A standard circular saw blade is just *7¼ inches* across, yet it slices a board in seconds.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: The motor spins the blade at roughly *5,500 RPM* with no load.

steps.label: Teeth
steps.text: Each *carbide-tipped tooth* chips off a little wood, and the gaps between teeth, called *gullets*, carry the sawdust out.

steps.label: Upcut
steps.text: The blade cuts *upward* from below, which pulls the board up against the saw's flat base plate.

steps.label: Guard
steps.text: A clear *spring-loaded guard* slides back as you push into the cut, then snaps shut over the blade.

steps.label: Adjust
steps.text: The base sets the cut *depth*, and tilts up to *45 degrees* for bevels.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, chip, *guard*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
